data_window: 2016-07-31..2026-07-19, 4 canary cells (fUST_a30, fUST_p2, fUSD_a30, fUSD_p2), daily-resampled
methodology: Reuses bfx_funding_bot.modules.backtest.signal_eda unmodified core (spearman_ic, block_bootstrap_ic, quintile_spread, bh_fdr, decide_signal, split_regime, add_forward_rate_change, resample_daily, build_signal_frame) against 2 new pure signal functions (frr_curvature, spike_pctile, added with unit tests) and 2 horizon-extension retests of the existing frr_trend/spike_z formulas. Data pulled read-only from the VM's self-hosted Postgres via a one-off docker container (--label autoheal=false, no deploy, no canary/live container touched), resampled to daily frames on the VM, then scp'd to a local scratch dir for the funnel run (kept the multi-minute compute off any DB session, same rationale as the original driver).

robustness_check.purpose: block_bootstrap_ic's block_size=20 default (from the 2026-06-06 ADR) was sized for H<=30d. At H=45/60/90 the forward-return target (mean of the next H days minus spot) overlaps (H-1)/H between consecutive rows -- a much longer induced serial-correlation length than block_size=20 can capture, which risks an artificially tight bootstrap CI/p-value on exactly the long-horizon observations this re-operationalization round depends on. This reruns the identical funnel with block_size=max(20, h) (block length scaled to the horizon) as a sensitivity check on the two extended-horizon signals.

conclusion: spike_z_extH (existing spike_z z-score formula, w=14, retested at H=45/60/90d instead of the original 2/7/14/30d) clears all 4 gates under BOTH the primary (block_size=20) and the block-size-robustness-check (block_size=max(20,h)) runs: 4/4 cells robust, same sign both disjoint regimes, FDR-significant, median IC -0.178 (floor 0.03). frr_trend_extH looked marginally promising under the primary block_size=20 run (2/4 cells robust) but that marginal significance evaporated under the robustness check (0 robust cells) -- demonstrating the robustness check is doing real work, not rubber-stamping. frr_curvature_k3 and spike_pctile_w14 are KILL under both runs (regime-fragile / underpowered early regime respectively, same failure mode as the original 2026-06-06 frr_trend/spike_detect KILLs).
